## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r}

setwd("~/BVG-7003/Devoir_1_BVG-7003/data/")
df = read.csv("~/BVG-7003/Devoir_1_BVG-7003/data/2_Data_RNASeq_Cannabis_Sex.csv")

library(dplyr)

REM16 <- dplyr::filter(df, grepl("LOC115699937", X))
FT1   <- dplyr::filter(df, grepl("LOC115696989", X))

female_cols <- grep("_XX", names(df), value = TRUE)
male_cols   <- grep("_XY", names(df), value = TRUE)

df_females_REM16 <- REM16[, c("X", female_cols)]
df_males_REM16   <- REM16[, c("X", male_cols)]

df_females_FT1   <- FT1[, c("X", female_cols)]
df_males_FT1     <- FT1[, c("X", male_cols)]

all_females_wide <- bind_rows(df_females_REM16, df_females_FT1)
all_males_wide   <- bind_rows(df_males_REM16, df_males_FT1)

females_long <- pivot_longer(all_females_wide, cols = -X, names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Expression")
females_long$Sex <- "Female (XX)"

males_long <- pivot_longer(all_males_wide, cols = -X, names_to = "Sample", values_to = "Expression")
males_long$Sex <- "Male (XY)"

df_final <- bind_rows(females_long, males_long)

```
## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r}

boxplot(Expression ~ Sex, 
        data = subset(df_final, X == "Cannabis_LOC115699937"),
        names = c("Femelle (XX)", "Mâle (XY)"),
        main = "Expression de REM16 selon le sexe",
        xlab = "Sexe", ylab = "Expression",
        col = c("pink", "lightblue"))

boxplot(Expression ~ Sex, 
        data = subset(df_final, X == "LOC115696989"),
        names = c("Femelle (XX)", "Mâle (XY)"),
        main = "Expression de FT1 selon le sexe",
        xlab = "Sexe", ylab = "Expression",
        col = c("pink", "lightblue"))

boxplot(Expression ~ Sex + X, 
        data = df_final,
        names = c("REM16\nFemelle (XX)", "REM16\nMâle (XY)", 
                  "FT1\nFemelle (XX)", "FT1\nMâle (XY)"),
        main = "Expression de REM16 et FT1 selon le sexe",
        xlab = "Gène et Sexe", ylab = "Expression",
        col = c("pink", "lightblue"))

```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
